title: The Endless Well
premise: Felix Brightwater returns to his grandmother's decaying farmhouse to bury his twin brother Theo, only to find that every photograph in the house now shows an extra chair at the kitchen table—and the chair is always empty, waiting. The family's old stories about the well behind the house, which 'counts' the living and takes what it is owed, turn out to be a ledger kept by something that has fed on the Brightwaters for generations. As relatives who never believed begin to vanish one by one, Felix must piece together his grandmother's hidden records and lead the fractured family out ahead of the count. In the end, Felix fills the well's debt by giving it the one thing it has always wanted—a willing memory, freely surrendered—and seals it at the cost of forgetting Theo entirely.
about_author: Rafael Vane is the pen name of a former rural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales across the American Midwest, where he collected more family photographs than he could ever explain. He writes horror about inheritance—of houses, debts, and things better left uncounted.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Felix arrives at the farmhouse for Theo's funeral, numb and disbelieving; the casket is closed and no one will say why. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into suspicion as he notices the family avoiding his eyes.

chapters.title: One Chair Too Many
chapters.summary: Sorting Theo's room, Felix finds childhood photos where an eleventh chair sits at the kitchen table—photos he remembers having ten chairs. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the first crack in his rationalism, dismissed but not forgotten.

chapters.title: Aunt Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Great-aunt Wren, sharp-tongued and half-blind, catches Felix photographing the pictures and warns him to stop counting. She shows him a ledger of names and dates going back two centuries. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread dressed as family eccentricity.

chapters.title: The Well Behind the House
chapters.summary: Felix visits the capped stone well despite warnings; the air above it is warm and smells of the kitchen. That night, every clock in the house reads the same wrong time. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Cousin Danny Counts Aloud
chapters.summary: Teenage cousin Danny, mocking the superstition, counts the family aloud at dinner—eleven. There are ten of them. Wren leaves the table without a word. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the horror becomes communal, undeniable.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Felix pries up the pantry floorboards and finds his grandmother's true records: not deaths, but trades—the well can be paid in memories instead of lives. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in guilt.

chapters.title: The First Vanishing
chapters.summary: Uncle Marlowe goes out to check the well cap and doesn't come back; his truck is there, his boots are there, and no one else remembers him clearly by morning. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror at how easily memory erases a man.

chapters.title: Nobody Remembers Marlowe
chapters.summary: The family holds no vigil for Marlowe because most cannot recall his face; only Felix and Wren fight to keep his name spoken. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: rage at the theft, and resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits she once paid the well a memory to save her sister, and it has been short ever since—waiting to balance its books. POV: Wren (brief shift) then Felix. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Photographs of the Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Felix studies decades of photos and realizes the extra chair appears only after each 'paid' memory—the well marks its accounts. He maps every debt against the family tree. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grim clarity; the pattern is real and nearly full.

chapters.title: Danny Runs
chapters.summary: Danny flees to town, but the road loops back to the farm no matter which way he drives; he returns hollow-eyed, whispering that the corn was counting him. POV: Danny. Emotional beat: claustrophobia—the house is not a place but a trap.

chapters.title: The Family Meeting
chapters.summary: Felix lays out the ledger before the surviving family and proposes they leave together, tonight, ahead of the count. Half refuse; the house itself groans in protest. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: leadership born unwillingly, fracturing the found-family bonds.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Dying
chapters.summary: Three relatives attempt to drive away; their car is found at the property line, engine warm, seats occupied by nothing. Those inside the house feel them slip from memory mid-sentence. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: despair—the well does not release what it counts.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Water sounds rise from beneath the capped stone at night; the kitchen tap runs cloudy and tastes of iron and old summers. Wren says the accounting is coming due. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: countdown pressure, the family huddling like survivors of a flood.

chapters.title: Theo's Room, Reopened
chapters.summary: Felix finally opens the sealed casket question: Theo's body was never in it. In Theo's room he finds a note in his brother's hand: 'It asked me first. I said yes.' POV: Felix. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: What Theo Gave
chapters.summary: Through grandmother's records, Felix learns Theo traded himself willingly to spare Felix—becoming the well's keeper, the eleventh chair. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: devastating love; the haunting was a gift all along.

chapters.title: Negotiating With the Water
chapters.summary: Felix speaks into the well at midnight, offering a trade: his own memories of Theo, freely given, to close the account forever. The water answers in Theo's voice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: temptation and sacrifice balanced on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: The Count Comes Due
chapters.summary: The well takes anyway—doors seal, water floods the cellar, and the family fights toward the attic as names begin dissolving from their minds. POV: alternating family members. Emotional beat: chaotic climax, love expressed as physically holding on to one another.

chapters.title: Eleven Chairs
chapters.summary: In the flooded kitchen, Felix sits in the eleventh chair and surrenders every memory of Theo—his face, his voice, their whole shared childhood—pouring it down the dark. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the climax's cost paid in the self.

chapters.title: Morning, Drained
chapters.summary: The well falls silent; the water recedes; the extra chair is gone from every photograph. The family walks out past the property line and the road simply continues. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: hollow relief, survival without wholeness.

chapters.title: The Man at the Funeral Home
chapters.summary: Weeks later, finalizing paperwork, Felix meets a stranger who feels achingly familiar and who thanks him quietly before walking into the rain. He weeps without knowing why. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief without object—love outlasting memory.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: The scattered family gathers each year at the farm, now theirs, keeping a chair set for someone no one can name. Felix begins writing everything down, so the well can never take the record twice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—found family choosing remembrance as resistance.
